sections.heading: StringBuffer vs StringBuilder in Java
paragraphs: Java provides three classes to represent a sequence of characters: String, StringBuffer, and StringBuilder. The String class is an immutable class whereas StringBuffer and StringBuilder classes are mutable. There are many differences between StringBuffer and StringBuilder. The StringBuilder class is introduced since JDK 1.5.

sections.heading: What is StringBuffer in Java?
paragraphs: StringBuffer is a mutable class that is used to create and modify strings without creating new objects. It is thread-safe that means, it is safe to use in multi-threaded environments.

sections.heading: What is StringBuilder in Java?
paragraphs: StringBuilder is a mutable class in Java similar to StringBuffer, but it is not thread-safe. It is faster than StringBuffer and it is commonly used in single-threaded applications.

sections.heading: Difference Between StringBuffer and StringBuilder Classes
paragraphs: A list of differences between StringBuffer and StringBuilder classes are given below:

StringBuffer | StringBuilder
StringBuffer is synchronized i.e. thread safe. It means two threads can't call the methods of StringBuffer simultaneously. | StringBuilder is non-synchronized i.e. not thread safe. It means two threads can call the methods of StringBuilder simultaneously.
StringBuffer is less efficient than StringBuilder. | StringBuilder is more efficient than StringBuffer.
StringBuffer was introduced in Java 1.0 | StringBuilder was introduced in Java 1.5
